learningObjective: Identify correct and incorrect statements about host/device synchronization in a CUDA-based ML runtime.
stem: Which statements about host/device synchronization in a CUDA runtime are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `cudaStreamSynchronize(stream)` blocks the calling host thread until all previously enqueued work on `stream` has completed, but does not affect work on other streams.
`cudaDeviceSynchronize()` waits for all streams on the current device to drain; overusing it in a hot loop serializes host and device and defeats stream-level overlap.

A `cudaMemcpyAsync` on the default stream is guaranteed to be fully overlapped with any kernel executing on another user-created stream, even without explicit event synchronization or the use of pinned host memory.

Under legacy default-stream semantics, `cudaMemcpy` (blocking) can be issued while a kernel is executing on a user-created stream and always returns immediately without waiting for that kernel — the two operations proceed independently.

explanation: A and B state the documented behavior of `cudaStreamSynchronize` and `cudaDeviceSynchronize`. C is wrong because overlap requires pinned host memory (page-locked) and appropriate stream separation — async doesn't guarantee overlap by itself. D reverses default-stream semantics: under legacy default-stream behavior, work on the default stream synchronizes with all other streams on the device (`cudaMemcpy` is blocking and will wait for prior work).

optionExplanations.B: Correct: overusing device-wide sync serializes execution.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: async is necessary but not sufficient for overlap — pinned memory and correct stream placement are also required.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: legacy default stream synchronizes with other streams; the blocking `cudaMemcpy` will wait for the kernel.

assumptions: CUDA runtime API in its documented behavior; legacy default-stream mode unless otherwise specified.
nonImplications: Does not imply per-thread default stream (`--default-stream per-thread`) has the same semantics; that mode changes the default-stream synchronization behavior.
Does not imply pinned memory is always desirable; it consumes physical RAM.

distractorRationales.C: Confuses async API with overlap guarantee.

sourceRefs.locator: Stream synchronization semantics; default stream behavior
Asynchronous memcpy and pinned memory requirement
